fields.h1: Build an Esthetician Intake Form That Arrives Before the Client
fields.hero_description: Describe what you ask before a facial or a wax. Emergent builds the esthetician intake form, the rules that act on each answer, and a client database you own.
fields.features_heading: What an Esthetician Intake Form Should Cover
fields.features_subheading: Six pieces that turn a clipboard of answers into a record the treatment room can use.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the service

Show each client only the section for the service she booked. A peel and a brow wax each carry their own questions, and nobody scrolls past the ones that never apply to her.
fields.feature_2:
A routine captured step by step

Ask for each product in the client's morning and evening routine on its own line, with how often she uses it. Actives such as retinoids and acids stand out on the treatment card.
fields.feature_3:
Skin concerns marked on a face map

Let clients tap the zones that bother them, such as the chin or the forehead, and pick a concern for each one. The map prints on the treatment card above the esthetician's notes.
fields.feature_4:
A refresh date on every form

Stamp each signed form with its date and decide how long it stays current. An older form adds an update link to that client's next reminder, sent by email the day before.
fields.feature_5:
Consent and photo release, signed

Close with your consent statement and an optional release for before-and-after photos, then collect a typed or drawn signature. Each signed copy is filed under its visit.
fields.feature_6:
Your form, as source code

Export the source of the intake form and its client database to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Run it on your own hosting, or have a developer connect it to your booking site.

fields.usecase_heading: Esthetician Intake Forms by Business Type
fields.tab_content_1:
Each product in her routine is on the facial card

New clients at Lumen Skin Studio enter their routine one product at a time. Morning and night get separate lists, with how often each product is used. Mara Quinn's facial card shows the routine beside the skin concerns the client marked. A nightly retinoid sits on the first line, where she reads it before picking a peel.
fields.tab_content_2:
Three more questions appear when she books microneedling

Northwind Med Spa runs one intake for its whole menu, and the service a client books decides what she sees. A hydrating facial goes from skin history to consent. Microneedling adds three questions about blood thinners, sun exposure and cold sores. Every answer is filed under that visit in one client record.
fields.tab_content_3:
After six months, the form asks again

Every form at Fernway Wax Bar carries the date it was signed. A regular whose form is more than six months old gets an update link in her reminder email. She answers the medication and skin questions again and skips the rest. At the desk, Theo Grant sees a green check beside her name once it is in.
fields.tab_content_4:
One link for a bridal party of six

Rosa Diaz does bridal facials at the hotel on the morning of the wedding. She sends one link to the bride, who forwards it to her party, and each guest fills in her own form on her phone. Two days before the wedding, Rosa's roster shows four forms in and two missing. The bride gets an email with the two names.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Esthetician Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Start with the services on your menu, then decide which answers should change a treatment before the client arrives.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the services on your menu
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the routine by product
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Flag answers worth a second look
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set how long a form stays current
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every service you offer and the questions each one needs. A facial and a microneedling session share contact details and skin history, but the second one needs extra questions before anyone picks up a needle.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each step of the home routine its own line: cleanser, serum, moisturizer, sunscreen. Ask how many times a week the client reaches for each one. One box labeled current products gets a shrug in reply, and an active like a retinoid goes unmentioned.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide which answers the esthetician must read before the client sits down, such as a prescription retinoid or a recent peel elsewhere. Move those to the top of the treatment card instead of halfway down page two.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the age at which a signed form needs an update and the questions that get asked again. Contact details rarely change between visits. Medications and skin conditions do, and those are the lines worth a fresh answer from a regular.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write out your services, the questions for each, and the answers that need a flag. Emergent builds the intake form, the client records it fills, and the email alerts. Adding a service later takes one more prompt, and the live form picks it up.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Close with a short consent statement and your cancellation policy in plain words, followed by a signature field. Keep each policy to a sentence or two. Have a lawyer in your state review the wording before any client signs it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send the link with the booking
fields.howto_step_7_des: Put the form link in the booking confirmation so answers arrive a day or more ahead. Fill it once as a test client who ticks every box and books each service, and confirm that each alert reaches the person it names.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template sites, Etsy and Pinterest listings, a client manager and a practice-software gallery, plus one survey builder. Each lists the same sections (contact details, medical history, medications, allergies, skin concerns, routine, consent) and stops at a blank form. This page treats the intake as the start of the treatment record: four esthetics businesses whose form shapes the appointment, a facial studio that reads the client's home routine before she sits down, a medical spa whose booked service decides which questions appear, a wax studio that asks again every six months, and a mobile esthetician who sends one link to a bridal party.
